description: Per-candidate backfill rows for #52 (track #50). Searched 2026-09-01 for material where Giannoulias says HOW, per the mechanism bar. What exists: his campaign site (alexiforchi.com) still has NO issues/platform page (About / News / Contact / Volunteer only) and its News page links only Secretary of State press clips - car insurance, libraries, e-bike safety, license plates - with zero housing content; the three podcast feeds in sources.json were pulled and grepped, as were the City Club / WTTW / WGN YouTube feeds; no candidate forum or housing questionnaire exists yet, a month into the race. The one untapped first-person source is row 3, his full Fran Spielman Show interview (recorded 07-31), and it is the only row here that carries policy mechanisms. What is excluded and why: Crain's and WGN 403 the fetcher; ABC7's 'trade jabs' piece has housing sentences that belong to the reporter and a campaign spokesperson, not to him (the #49 attribution trap); and the Sun-Times writeup of the same Spielman interview was run and then dropped - its extraction produced a fragment of the reporter's own sentence quoted as his ('universal pre-K, property tax reform and raising the minimum wage'), a CPS-funding line mis-flagged as housing, and a remark about CHA going a year without a leader, which is a governance complaint rather than a housing position. Record: one targeted pass found nothing. Secretary of State (2023-) does not intersect housing and the Treasurer years fall outside the 2016-01-01 recency cutoff, so an empty record array is the honest outcome, not a failed backfill. Rows 1-2 are the launch-day press already merged in #66/#73, kept as the row list of record; only row 3 was run for this PR (write_stance unions citations across sources since #72, so re-running 1-2 was unnecessary and would risk superseding verified statements with a non-deterministic re-extraction).

rows.title: Backed by Trade Unions, Alexi Giannoulias Launches Campaign for Chicago Mayor
Illinois Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias announces campaign for Chicago mayor
